updates.title: Artemis III is now a docking-heavy Earth-orbit mission — and NASA just filled in key details
updates.subtitle: A closer look at the new spacer, the LEO architecture, and what NASA still has to decide before crews start training.
updates.summary: NASA published the most concrete public outline yet for Artemis III: an Earth-orbit rehearsal, a non-propulsive SLS spacer, and rendezvous/docking tests with Starship HLS and Blue Moon pathfinders.
updates.author: Joachim Gresslien

updates.title: Reid Wiseman Needed to Hug an Engineer
updates.subtitle: Artemis II’s heat shield came back cleaner than Artemis I — and NASA still has work to do before Artemis III.
updates.summary: Artemis II’s post-flight heat shield imagery suggests NASA’s re-entry changes worked — but the hardest validation work for Artemis III is still ahead.
updates.author: Joachim Gresslien

updates.title: Artemis III: The Rocket Is Moving, the Plan Isn't
updates.subtitle: Two months after NASA's mission rewrite, several core questions about Artemis III still don't have public answers.
updates.summary: NASA still hasn't named a crew, an orbit, or a duration for Artemis III — and the launch date is quietly drifting toward late 2027. Here's why a modest slip removes one of the two planned 2028 lunar landings.
updates.author: Joachim Gresslien

updates.title: Artemis II: Everything That Floated Past the Moon
updates.subtitle: Iconic photographs, an hour-long eclipse, an emotional crater dedication — and one small plush toy carrying 5.6 million names. The full story.
updates.summary: What really happened during Artemis II's ten days in deep space. Including the part with the toilet, the eight-year-old who shipped 5.6 million names to the Moon, and the moment the crew broke down.
updates.author: Joachim Gresslien

updates.title: 6 Things NASA Just Figured Out About Going to the Moon
updates.subtitle: The post-flight data from Artemis II is in — and some of the findings surprised even the engineers who designed the hardware.
updates.summary: Thermal margins exceeded predictions. Astronauts adapted faster than Apollo crews. And one engineering fix worked better than expected. Inside the Artemis II debrief.
updates.author: Joachim Gresslien

updates.title: The $228 Million Moon Suit Prada Helped Design
updates.subtitle: NASA outsourced the most iconic garment in human exploration to a fashion house and a startup. Here's what that looks like.
updates.summary: For the first time ever, NASA astronauts will walk on the Moon in a privately-built spacesuit — co-designed by Italian fashion house Prada.
updates.author: Joachim Gresslien

updates.title: The Moon Landing That Needs 12 Refueling Flights
updates.subtitle: Before any Artemis III astronaut even leaves Earth, SpaceX must solve an orbital refueling problem no one has ever attempted. The stakes could not be higher.
updates.summary: Exclusive deep dive: why NASA's safety panel, the Inspector General, and a former administrator all think Artemis III could be years late.
updates.author: Joachim Gresslien
